card.name: Digits and punctuation in medical references
card.fires_on: Numbers and punctuation inside medical references, such as the dot in 'Clinical Studies (14.3)', digits in zip codes of health agencies, and birth years of physicians. The pole responds on the digit or dot itself.

modes.label: Clinical Studies section numbers
modes.description: The dot after 14 in cross-references to the Clinical Studies section of a drug label.
modes.example: exon 18 mutation [see Clinical Studies (14<<.>>1) ] . Information on the FDA

modes.label: Digits in health agency addresses
modes.description: A digit inside a zip code in the address of a health agency such as NIH or FDA.
modes.example: WATCH, Food and Drug Administration (FDA), 5600 Fishers Lane, Rockville, MD 20852-9<<7>>82. Telephone: (80

modes.label: Dates and reviewer credits
modes.description: A digit in a physician's birth year or the colon after 'Reviewed By' in a medical review line.
modes.example: stone; 2008:chap 164. |Review Date: 2/8/2012| Reviewed By<<:>> Todd Gersten, MD, Hematology

card.writes: It pushes medical and clinical words, mostly Chinese ones, and suppresses engineering, metal and gas words.
card.plain: It fires on numbers and punctuation in medical citations and addresses, and makes the model expect medical wording next.
